name: Automate health insurance claim intake in openIMIS
demonstrates: A health-facility claim entered once in openIMIS - the open-source system used by national health-insurance schemes - compiled, and replayed with a fresh claim number, accepted only when a direct SQL read shows exactly one new claim row in status Entered for the right policyholder and facility.

install.note: Installs the OpenAdapt launcher, compiler, and browser capability.

tryItCommand: openadapt flow record --url http://localhost:8000/ --out rec && openadapt flow compile rec --out bundle --name claim-intake

runStats.sourceLabel: Reference environment replays (deliberately not a benchmark)
runStats.environment: openIMIS 25.10 from digest-pinned images with the upstream synthetic demo dataset; everything binds to localhost
runStats.comparisonArm: Separate small-N paid-agent run on a different flow build: 3/3 correct, 0/3 over-halt, 0/3 silent incorrect, $0.4793 per run; no matched timing matrix, so no comparative claim is made
runStats.measuredOn: compiled arm on openadapt-flow 1.11.0 (evidence committed 2026-07-17); agent arm on openadapt-flow 1.19.0 (2026-07-21)

faq.question: What failure does the SQL oracle catch?
faq.answer: The costly one: the claim silently entered twice, or against the wrong policyholder, surfacing weeks later in reconciliation. A duplicate or missing claim row fails the run loudly instead of reporting success.

faq.question: Is this a benchmark result?
faq.answer: No. The repository describes it as a reference environment, deliberately not a benchmark: there is no matched timing matrix or publication protocol behind the 3/3 compiled replays.
